output.summary: Volume was flat (-0.9%), and the cost-per-bushel gain comes entirely from maintenance cut 2.8 to 1.9 cents. The deferred backlog is 3.1 times the FY2024 level, with safety and dust items concentrated at Harlan Junction. The insurer found critical hazards there and set a 21 November deadline. So the efficiency claim looks like deferred maintenance, and the readiness claim is not supported. The revenue driver is unestablished: no price or merchandising data was collected. Viability of the expansion is unknown. Superintendent dependence is plausible but has no controlled comparison. Fix the hazards now, start knowledge capture, and defer the vote until the financial case is rebuilt. Holding maintenance at $612K and extending the hiring freeze would be harmful.
